card.title: Wildlife: Importance, Causes of Extinction and Conservation Strategies

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Wildlife underpins ecosystem function and human well-being, yet faces severe threats from habitat loss, overexploitation, invasive species, and climate change. Effective conservation combines legal frameworks, protected areas, captive breeding, and community engagement.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Wildlife means undomesticated organisms, not only large mammals.
It matters for pollination, seed dispersal, soil, tourism and for its own sake.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Extinction and endangerment are the same. ✅ Extinct means no living individuals remain; endangered means at high risk of extinction.  ·  ❌ Poaching and hunting are identical. ✅ Hunting may be legal and regulated; poaching is illegal.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Wildlife = non-domesticated organisms in natural habitats  ·  Ecosystem services: pollination, seed dispersal, nutrient cycling  ·  Leading extinction cause: habitat destruction  ·  Other causes: overexploitation, invasive species, pollution, climate change

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Over 1 million species are currently threatened with extinction (IPBES)  ·  Habitat loss affects ~85% of threatened species

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Wildlife includes all non-domesticated plants, animals, and microorganisms living in natural habitats, forming essential components of ecosystems.  ·  Wildlife provides ecosystem services: pollination, seed dispersal, nutrient cycling, pest control, and maintenance of food webs.  ·  Wildlife has economic value through ecotourism, medicinal resources, genetic diversity for agriculture, and sustainable harvest of timber and non-timber products.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Strategies: legal protection, protected areas, captive breeding, restoration  ·  CITES regulates international wildlife trade  ·  ❌ Invasive species always increase biodiversity. ✅ They usually reduce native biodiversity.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Nepal's wildlife is protected under National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act 1973  ·  Wildlife holds cultural, aesthetic, and ethical value, supporting indigenous knowledge and spiritual traditions.  ·  Major causes of extinction: habitat destruction and fragmentation, overexploitation (hunting, poaching), invasive species, pollution, climate change, and disease.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Habitat loss is the leading cause of species extinction, driven by deforestation, agriculture, urbanization, and infrastructure development.  ·  Overexploitation occurs when harvesting exceeds reproduction rates, as seen in ivory poaching and overfishing.  ·  Invasive alien species outcompete native species for resources and alter ecosystem dynamics (e.g., Lantana camara in Nepal).
